deep.reconstruction:
CONTEXT. The previous page computes zeta(1/2) = -1.4602945..., xi(0), and the saddle-point relation dn/dalpha = (1/2pi) log(alpha/2pi). This page belongs to Riemann's derivation of the asymptotic correction terms in what is now called the Riemann–Siegel formula. In the integrand x^{-s} e^{pi i x^2}/(e^{pi i x}-e^{-pi i x}) one writes s = 1/2 + it. Expanding about the saddle point gives the factor (1+y/alpha)^{alpha^2/(2pi i) - 1/2}, so that -s = alpha^2/(2pi i) - 1/2, i.e. t = alpha^2/(2pi). Hence alpha = sqrt(2 pi t) = 2pi times Siegel's a = sqrt(t/2pi).

(A) Key expansion. Riemann writes log(1+y/alpha) = y/alpha - y^2/(2alpha^2) + y^3/(3alpha^3) - ... From this:
E(y) := exp(-alpha y/(2pi i) + y^2/(4pi i)) (1+y/alpha)^{alpha^2/(2pi i)} = exp( y^3/(6pi i alpha) - y^4/(8 pi i alpha^2) + y^5/(10 pi i alpha^3) - ... ).
The linear and quadratic terms cancel (my computation). The residual factor (1+y/alpha)^{-1/2} adds -y/(2alpha) + ... to the exponent. The integral he studies is
J = ∫ eta(y) E(y) (1+y/alpha)^{-1/2} dy, with E(y)(1+y/alpha)^{-1/2} = Σ a_n y^n.
The leading part is exp(c y^3/alpha) with c = ±1/(6 pi i).

(B) Lines 1–4: turning a series in derivatives into an integral operator (Borel–Laplace device). Two standard facts are used:
- (1/2pi i)∮ f(x+z) z^{-k-1} dz = f^{(k)}(x)/k!.
- ∫_0^∞ e^{-u} (u/z)^k du = k! z^{-k}.
Hence for g(w) = Σ c_k w^k one has formally
(1/2pi i)∮ f(x+z) [∫_0^∞ e^{-u} g(u/z) du] dz/z = Σ c_k f^{(k)}(x).
Riemann applies this to g(w) = exp(-(1/alpha) w^3/(6pi i)). The n-th term is (-1)^n w^{3n}/(n! (6 pi i alpha)^n). Combined with ∫ e^{-x} x^{3n} dx = Π(3n), this gives line 1: ∫ f(x+z) z^{-3n-1} dz · Π(3n)/(n! 6^n (pi i)^n alpha^n) (up to sign and the 2pi i normalisation).
A next-order correction term (involving x^5/z^5 and alpha^2, 2^4·5) is written and struck out. It is replaced by a coefficient formula for z^{-3n+3}:
Π(3n-4)(3n-1) / ((n-2)! 6^{n-2} 2^{3n-2}·5 (pi i)^{n-1} alpha^{n-2}).
This is evidently the general coefficient of a mixed term (powers of the cubic times a higher-order term). I could not reconstruct its exact origin with certainty.

(C) Duality argument. Set e^{2pi i z^2} f(x+z) = Σ b_n z^n = ∫ eta(y) e^{2zy} dy. Comparing coefficients gives ∫ y^n eta dy = b_n Π(n)/2^n (correct). Therefore
J = Σ a_n ∫ y^n eta dy = Σ a_n b_n Π(n)/2^n.
The same sum is recovered from a Laplace integral:
∫_0^∞ e^{-y} Σ a_n (y/2z)^n dy = Σ Π(n) a_n (2z)^{-n}.
Its integrand is written explicitly as exp(-y - (alpha/2z) y/(2pi i) + (y/2z)^2/(4pi i)) (1 + y/(2 alpha z))^{alpha^2/(2pi i) - 1/2}. Multiplying by e^{2pi i z^2} f(x+z) and integrating (1/2pi i)∮ ... dz/z picks out Σ a_n b_n Π(n)/2^n = J. So J is expressed as a double integral in z and y.

(D) Completing the square. He writes
-y - alpha y/(2z·2pi i) + (y/2z)^2/(4pi i) = (1/4pi i)(y/2z - alpha - 4pi i z)^2 - (alpha + 4pi i z)^2/(4pi i).
This is correct.
He then replaces the Gaussian factor by the limit form (1 - u/n)^{-n^2/(4pi i)} (1 + u/n)^{-n^2/(4pi i)}, which tends to e^{u^2/(4pi i)} as n → ∞, with u = y/2z - alpha - 4pi i z.
The integrand thus becomes a product of three powers of linear functions of y. Its branch points are:
- y = 2alpha z + 8 pi i z^2 ± 2nz (from u = ±n, correct);
- y = -2 alpha z.
This is the setting of Riemann's P-function, i.e. a hypergeometric integral with three finite singular points; the confluent limit is n → ∞. The exponents are noted as (n(2alpha + 4 pi i z) ± 1)/2.

(E) Model problem. He considers ∫_{-∞} e^{t^2} (1+t/x)^alpha dt and expands (1+t/x)^alpha = Σ Π(alpha)/(Π(n)Π(alpha-n)) t^n/x^n. Only even powers survive, with Gaussian moments giving Π(n-1/2) up to constants. The result is the asymptotic series Σ Π(alpha) Π(n-1/2)/(Π(2n) Π(alpha-2n)) x^{-2n}.
The reflection formula turns Π(alpha)/Π(alpha-2n) into a multiple of Π(2n-alpha-1). Legendre duplication then gives Π(2n-alpha-1) Π(n-1/2)/Π(2n) = 2^{-alpha-1} Π(n - alpha/2 - 1/2) Π(n - alpha/2 - 1)/Π(n) (verified).
The series is therefore a 2F0(-alpha/2, 1/2 - alpha/2; ; const/x^2), a parabolic-cylinder-type function. Riemann identifies it with a P-symbol:
P{0, 1/2 - alpha/2, 0; c, -alpha/2, -c + alpha + 1/2}.
The exponent sum is 1, as Riemann's condition requires. With gamma = 1 - c this is 2F1(1/2 - alpha/2, -alpha/2; 1 - c; w), and the 2F0 arises as the confluent limit c → ∞ with suitably scaled argument (my interpretation).

(F) Final block. The same double integral is taken with rescaled variables:
(1/2pi i)∮ f(x+z) e^{2pi i z^2} 2 dz ∫_0^∞ e^{-2zy - alpha y/(2pi i) + y^2/(4pi i)} (1+y)^{alpha^2/(2pi i) - 1/2} dy.
He shifts y → y - (alpha + 4pi i z), using -2zy - alpha y/(2pi i) + y^2/(4pi i) = (y^2 - 2y(alpha + 4pi i z))/(4pi i). The inner integral becomes
e^{2pi i z^2 - (alpha + 4pi i z)^2/(4pi i)} ∫_{-(alpha + 4pi i z)}^∞ e^{y^2/(4pi i)} (alpha + 4 pi i z + 1 + y)^{alpha^2/(2pi i) - 1/2} dy.
This is correct. The page ends with an unfinished 'df/dz ='.
errors: Line 1 normalisation: the n-th coefficient of exp(±w^3/(6 pi i alpha)) is (±1)^n/(n!(6 pi i alpha)^n); depending on how the ink is read ('2pi i^n'), a factor 2^n or a sign may be off. Line 3 uses (pi i)^{n-1}, which supports 6^n (pi i)^n.

The sign of the cubic term: from the expansion one gets +y^3/(6 pi i alpha), while line 2 seems to carry -(1/alpha)(x/z)^3/(6 pi i). This is harmless if the orientation y → -y is intended, but it is not stated.

The struck-out correction term (x^5/(z^5 alpha^2 pi i 2^4·5)) does not match the obvious next terms of the expansion (-y^4/(8 pi i alpha^2), -y/(2alpha), y^5/(10 pi i alpha^3)). Riemann likely noticed this and crossed it out. The replacement coefficient for z^{-3n+3} could not be verified.

All series manipulations (termwise Laplace transform, interchange of the z and y integrals) are formal: the series Σ a_n y^n gives only asymptotic, generally divergent, expansions. No convergence justification is given.

In (E) the Gaussian moment constants (sqrt(pi), and the sign/rotation needed for e^{+t^2}) and the reflection-formula sign (-1)^{2n}·sin factor are suppressed. This is acceptable as 'up to constant factors'.

results.what: Cancellation of the linear and quadratic terms in exp(-alpha y/(2pi i) + y^2/(4pi i))(1+y/alpha)^{alpha^2/(2pi i)}, leaving exp(y^3/(6 pi i alpha) + ...): the saddle-point expansion for zeta(1/2+it) with t = alpha^2/2pi
results.modern_name: saddle-point (steepest descent) expansion in the Riemann–Siegel formula
results.usually_credited_to: Riemann (Nachlass), published by C. L. Siegel 1932

results.what: Representing a formal series Σ c_k f^{(k)}(x) as (1/2pi i)∮ f(x+z) ∫_0^∞ e^{-u} g(u/z) du dz/z (Cauchy formula combined with Laplace/Borel transform)
results.modern_name: Borel–Laplace transform / Borel summation of a differential-operator series
results.usually_credited_to: Borel (1899) for Borel summation; operational use common in 19th c.

results.what: Duality J = Σ a_n b_n n!/2^n via e^{2pi i z^2} f(x+z) = ∫ eta e^{2zy} dy, turning the correction terms into a double contour/Laplace integral
results.modern_name: Hadamard-product / moment representation; Riemann–Siegel correction terms C_j as combinations of derivatives of Psi
results.usually_credited_to: Riemann via Siegel 1932 (C_j as derivatives of Psi); this specific integral representation unsure

results.what: Approximating the Gaussian e^{u^2/(4pi i)} by (1-u^2/n^2)^{-n^2/(4pi i)}, making the integrand a product of powers (hypergeometric type) with a confluent limit

Asymptotic series of ∫ e^{t^2}(1+t/x)^alpha dt, reduced by reflection and duplication to Π(n-alpha/2-1/2)Π(n-alpha/2-1)/Π(n) x^{-2n}, i.e. a 2F0 identified with a P-symbol {0, 1/2-alpha/2, 0; c, -alpha/2, -c+alpha+1/2}
results.modern_name: parabolic cylinder / 2F0 asymptotic series as a confluent limit of 2F1
results.usually_credited_to: Weber/Hermite (parabolic cylinder functions); confluent hypergeometric theory Kummer/Whittaker

deep.surprise_reason: The general setting (saddle-point expansion behind the Riemann–Siegel formula, with correction terms built from derivatives of Psi) is known from Siegel's 1932 publication of Riemann's Nachlass. The specific Borel–Laplace operator representation of the derivative series and the explicit link to Riemann's P-function by confluence are notable unpublished working details. Some of this was perhaps not described in full by Siegel, but it is not a major new theorem.
